content:
jeff: FYI CI perf flagged PR #20888 — throughput_unit_test dropped below threshold on the mainline job: https://ci/reports/7342129999
ci-bot: Build 7342129999-PR-20888 failed: perf-threshold (throughput_unit_test). See artifacts/logs.tar.gz
maya: which metric and how big of a delta?
jeff: short log: 
```
FAILED: throughput_unit_test
Expected >= 1200 tps, got 1120 tps (-6.7%)
summary: median_tokens_per_sec down ~7% vs golden
note: kernel_selector chose 'matmul_fallback' for seq=512
```
olivia: hmm kernel_selector choosing fallback is suspicious — we've seen that cost-table tweaks can flip selection for mid-length sequences
ren: also saw KV cache hitrate drop in the job: 87% -> 72% (same workload snapshot) — could compound latency/throughput
sam: did any of the recent PRs touch the kernel cost estimates or sampler stats? PR 20750 changed the cost model for int8 matmul IIRC
maya: I'll run a local bisect between main@HEAD and merge of 20750 -> 20888 to isolate. running `scripts/ci-bisect --range=20700..20900 --bench=throughput_unit_test`
jeff: adding profiler flamegraph excerpt from the failing run: 
```
kernel_selector.cpp:hot     48.2%
matmul_fallback            30.1%
optimized_matmul           12.4%
batcher                    5.3%
kv_cache                   4.0%
```
olivia: that flamegraph lines up — selector hot path dominates and falls back to slower kernel. quick mitigation: pin kernel selection for seq in [256,1024] to `optimized_matmul` on canary (hotfix) or revert the cost-table change in 20750
ren: I can reproduce the KV hit drop locally when selector flips kernels — looks like different kernel layout changes padding leading to lower KV prefix matches
maya: bisect job started; will report which commit flips the metric. if bisect shows 20750, I'll prepare a revert PR for 20750 in canary and run the perf suite before rolling out
sam: +1 gate the rollout. hold canary until we verify. also add targeted microbench matrix: seq=[128,256,512,1024], batch=[1,4,8], quant=[fp16,int8]
jeff: plan: (1) maya bisect (2) if repro -> revert 20750 from canary (3) run targeted microbench (4) add unit test to assert kernel-selector monotonicity for cost deltas
ci-bot: Created perf/issue-20888: "throughput drop on PR 20888 - possible kernel-selector cost flip" — https://tracker/perf/20888
maya: will update thread when bisect finishes, should be ~30–45m
jeff: thanks — tagging @olivia @ren for followups, :thumbsup:
